allOf.$comment: CHK-01 Full governed record: every §3.4 content group must be present.
CHK-02 Field-removal ablation is defined only over the full governed record.
CHK-03 Ablated component must be absent: rationale.
CHK-04 Ablated component must be absent: scope (and with it, exclusions).
CHK-05 Ablated component must be absent: authority.
CHK-06 Ablated component must be absent: retainedDissent.
CHK-07 Ablated component must be absent: provenance.
CHK-08 Ablated component must be absent: lifecycle (lifecycle status).
CHK-09 Between-condition arm label_only is a deliberate degradation.
CHK-10 Between-condition arm unstructured_comment adds free text only.
CHK-11 Between-condition arm structured_provenance carries structure and lineage but no governance layer.
CHK-12 Only lifecycle state active may leave the record-side reuse gate open.
CHK-13 State active implies the record-side reuse gate is open. C3's read-side gates apply on top and are not decided here.
CHK-14 Retained dissent that is qualified and not yet adjudicated forces state retained_dissent.
CHK-15 Revocation requires a recorded reason and a revoking authority.
CHK-16 Supersession requires a named successor record.
CHK-17 Expiry requires a recorded expiry timestamp and the condition that fired.

CHK-18 State active requires a claim-specific competence assessment and a claim-scoped authority. Suspended under a declared field-removal ablation, so that a struck component is not reported as non-conformance.

ablation.$comment: Field-removal hooks for §3.4 Phase B. withheldComponents names top-level properties an ablation harness deletes.

decisionTrace.$comment: §3.4 p.17 and §2.2 p.12. Six named slots, surfaced to the reviewer at judgment time. Explicitly NOT hidden chain-of-thought.

verdict.$comment: System-independent via declared vocabulary indirection: no verdict term is hard-coded in the contract.

rationale.$comment: Structured so a field-removal ablation can strike it whole, and so each assertion links to a decision-trace slot.

counterevidenceEntry.$comment: Evidence that cut against the reviewer's own conclusion.

scope.$comment: §3.4 'scope and exclusions'. Scope is a decidable conjunction over declared context dimensions; exclusions are the negative half.

competence.$comment: §1.8 p.10-11. Claim-specific assessed competence, recorded separately from authority. An aggregate profile may be referenced but cannot satisfy claimSpecific.

authority.$comment: §1.8 p.10-11 and §3.4 p.17. Claim-scoped mandate to settle this contested fragment, recorded separately from competence.

visibility.$comment: SQ2 specifies what visibility contains; SQ3 decides when it is evaluated. Default is deny.

validation.$comment: Validation evidence is retained on the record rather than discarded at ingest.

disagreement.$comment: Detection and adjudication apparatus. The dissenting judgments themselves live in retainedDissent.

dissentEntry.$comment: §3.4 p.17: conflicting qualified judgments are kept, not averaged. Entries are append-only and are annotated by adjudication, never deleted.

provenance.$comment: §3.4 'provenance and version history'. Records are immutable; an amendment is a new record linked by lineage.

lifecycle.$comment: §3.4 Figure 12. Enumerated states, enumerated legal transitions, and a derived record-side reuse gate.

transitionRecord.$comment: Both accepted transitions and rejected attempts are recorded, so predictable rejection is inspectable.

allOf.$comment: Legal transition table. TXX is reserved for a rejected attempt at a pair that is not in the table.

receipts.$comment: §3.4 'later retrieval, use, and outcome receipts'. Append-only side log; the arrays are the snapshot projection.

outcomeReceipt.$comment: Instrumentation hook only. Presence of a field is not a measurement and carries no outcome claim.

bindings.$comment: §3.4 p.17: bound to the exact system and artifact versions, so a later reader can determine what was actually inspected.
